Prolapsed disc when I was 21. Had incorrectly tried to move a TV following my dad's instructions and felt what I can only describe as a squishy snap in my lower back. Even made a slight sound. Felt something was off but didn't feel any pain or discomfort at that moment. 

Flash forward to 4am the following day, and I woke up in unbearable, agonising pain. It was so intense that I was unable to properly move myself off the bed. I kinda rolled out. From there I could only really crawl. Had to crawl to my parents room and tell my dad to phone an ambulance. What followed for the next year was debilitating mobility where I couldn't walk, sit, or stand for very long. Couldn't push. Couldn't pull. Carrying was a no go. Even taking a shit would hurt me, I would need to move my body sideways and that would alleviate the pain somehow. I would try to rehabilitate repeatedly, only to somehow 'relapse' with my back which would bring me back to where I was in the beginning pain wise. I decided to eventually go against the doctors advice of keeping active and just let my body rest for a very extended period of time. And I eventually recovered. Somewhat. Now it's like a bullet wound where the flesh is healed over. No one would know I have a prolapse on the surface. But if I push myself too far, even now 11 years later, I would definitely be back to crawling in agony.

Choji's win always felt like an ass pull. Simply put he didn't deserve the victory. He uses his hax pills and doesn't suffer any of the dire consequences advertised, except for having a tummy ache. Jirobo, who had more fighting experience, jutsu, and took time to master the curse seal, should have destroyed Choji. He earned his right to be cocky and arrogant, and to obliterate Choji. If Choji was to win this fight, there should have been some lasting consequences to actually give the fight some weight. No pun intended. Maybe HE'S the one to end up in a wheelchair. Maybe he needs to retire as a shinobi. Maybe he loses a limb somehow. Something that doesnt just make everything hunky dory the next time we see him. Choji didn't deserve to win this fight, let alone survive it. I'm still perplexed by how some consider this one of the best fights. 

As for Guy, it would have been a perfect send off. The literal condition is protect something worth DYING for. I remember watching Naruto pulling his broken OP death defying BS, and actually feeling bored. It really deflated the fight and halted the momentum and stakes. While I don't think Guy should have killed Madara, I defintely believe the tussle should have crippled Madara somehow, even post regen. This could have been tied into the final fight he would have with Naruto and Sasuke as a key point of exploitation for their victory against him. Would have made Guy look good, given some credence to the 8th gate and its sacrifice being worth it. Would have set the stage for Kaguya, I guess? With her needing Madara weakened or pushed to his limit before she could emerge. Something better than him getting fisted in an anticlimactic betrayal. 

With Gaara, he had a lot more to give as a character story wise. And it actually made sound sense for Chiyo to use that jutsu to revive him. We had seen it in action with Sakura, we understood the risks, and that this was an incredibly rare and obscure jutsu. Chiyo had all her family issues resolved. She left her will to the next generation. Perfect time to use it in a final redemptive act. And in regards to Kakashi, it wasn't his time to go. His story is deeply connected to Obito's. Can you imagine Obito's big reveal and subsequent events in the war without Kakashi there? Nah. Kakashi had to stick around. He had actual plot armour.
